cross_modal_consistency.dimension_interpretation: Partition-level structural diagnostics provide triage evidence only. The internal screen shows a dominant single-cluster resolution in all three sets (candidate_k=1, large leading eigengaps 0.80-0.96 with sharp drop-off), so no obvious internal subdivision signal is present at screening resolution. Within-set affinities (0.51-0.68) exceed between-set affinities (0.22-0.24), and the nearest competing pair is S1-S2. This pattern is coherent at the partition level but does not by itself establish biological meaning, clinical validity, or any accept/drop/split/merge action.
cross_modal_consistency.cross_evidence_context: No prior reports were supplied; this is the sole partition-level structural diagnostic in the current round. The geometry basis is candidate-generation consensus, which is not external validation or a stability score.
limitations: Partition-level screening does not provide actual feasible k>=2 solutions or their measurements; absence of a subdivision signal is neither positive nor negative evidence about independence from neighboring candidates.
Nearest-pair affinities are a pair-review entry point, not a merge conclusion.

cross_modal_consistency.dimension_interpretation: For this candidate pair, the four native patient geometries provide weak and materially conflicting boundary representation. RNA shows the clearest (though still modest) separation (silhouette 0.159, negative fraction 0.131) and WSI shows weak positive separation (silhouette 0.118, negative fraction 0.393), whereas CT (silhouette 0.016, negative fraction 0.377) and WXS (silhouette 0.025, negative fraction 0.328) show essentially no separation. Synthesized jointly rather than by vote counting, the overall native-view pattern provides weak, conflicting evidence that the boundary between these two sets is expressed in the available geometries: two views show modest separation while two show none, and negative fractions of 0.13-0.39 indicate a substantial minority of patients are closer to the competing label than to their own. This does not itself determine whether the pair should be merged and does not establish biological meaning or clinical validity.
cross_modal_consistency.cross_evidence_context: The partition-level structural screen reported within-set affinities exceeding between-set affinities with S1-S2 as the nearest competing pair, so this S1-C0003 pair is not the nearest competing pair. The transcriptomic report for S2 shows a coherent metabolic-oxidative phenotype, but that is a set-versus-rest contrast and does not directly address this pair boundary. No confounder report is available.
limitations: Native-view alignments are current-label representations in each modality's own geometry, not independent validation or mechanistic agreement.
Material cross-modal disagreement: CT and WXS show negligible separation while RNA and WSI show modest separation.
Negative fractions of 0.13-0.39 indicate a substantial minority of patients are not closer to their own label.
Modalities are synthesized jointly; strong support in one view does not override material disagreement in others, and disagreement does not automatically invalidate the candidate.

cross_modal_consistency.dimension_interpretation: For this set, the four native patient geometries provide coherent, though modest, positive membership representation. All four views have positive mean silhouettes: WSI is the clearest (0.301, negative fraction 0.071), with RNA (0.091, 0.179), WXS (0.095, 0.179), and CT (0.032, 0.286) showing weaker positive separation. Synthesized jointly rather than by vote counting, the overall native-view pattern provides coherent but modest evidence that current membership is expressed in the available geometries, with negative fractions of 7.1-28.6% indicating a minority of patients are closer to a competing label. The nearest competing set differs by view: CT and WXS point to S1, while RNA and WSI point to S2, consistent with this set sitting between the two S1/S2 candidates in the partition. This bears on membership representation but does not by itself determine accept or drop and does not establish biological meaning or clinical validity.
cross_modal_consistency.cross_evidence_context: Prior partition-level structural diagnostics reported within-set affinities exceeding between-set affinities with nearest competing pair S1-S2, and prior pair-level reports for S1-K3_C0003 and S2-K3_C0003 described weak, partially conflicting boundary representation. The set-level native-view pattern here is the most coherent of the three sets, with all four views positive, though modest. Prior biological reports for this set (weak-to-moderate, non-robust mutation phenotype) are a separate evidence dimension and do not alter this geometry interpretation.

biological_support.dimension_interpretation: This set shows a weak-to-moderate mutation phenotype relative to the rest of the current partition. PBRM1 is the strongest driver-panel signal (OR 3.72, p=0.0057, set 17/28 vs rest 22/75) and VHL is nominally enriched (OR 2.71, p=0.045), but neither survives within-driver-panel FDR (q_driver=0.085 and 0.227) or global FDR (q_global=1.0). BAP1 trends toward depletion (OR 0.081, p=0.018, q_driver=0.133). Most other drivers are null, and CDKN2A is not estimable because neither group has events. Exploratory top genes show nominal enrichment with extremely wide intervals and no global significance. Overall the mutation profile does not provide a coherent, multiplicity-robust molecular program distinguishing this set; it characterizes biological identity only and does not establish that current membership, boundary, or granularity deserves independent retention.
biological_support.cross_evidence_context: The partition-level structural screen reported a dominant single-cluster resolution with no internal subdivision signal. No transcriptomic pathway report is available for this set to cross-check the mutation profile. The nominal PBRM1/VHL enrichment is directionally consistent with a ccRCC driver context but does not survive multiplicity adjustment.
limitations: Set-versus-rest contrast in a three-set partition: the rest combines multiple candidate sets and may be heterogeneous.
Driver panel is a post-hoc prespecified ccRCC biological annotation, not a discovery feature-selection criterion.
q_driver (within-driver-panel FDR) must not be conflated with q_global (FDR across the complete tested-gene family).
Exploratory top genes are a limited display subset only; every interpretation-matrix gene participates in q_global.
Zero-cell Haldane-Anscombe correction was applied to some odds ratios and intervals; Fisher p-values use the original uncorrected table.
CDKN2A is not estimable (no events in either group); non-estimability is neither support nor contradiction.
Biological identity does not by itself establish that current membership, boundary, or granularity deserves independent retention.
